title: H L A genes and drug hypersensitivity

segs.text: Section twenty one. Immune system variants, the H L A genes and drug hypersensitivity. She called this the newest and hottest area of pharmacogenomics. Certain H L A variants identify people at risk for severe, sometimes fatal, hypersensitivity reactions, immune reactions to specific drugs. Many biologicals now on the market have immunologically based side effects, some autoimmune, that are hard to predict; as more biologicals arrive, more variants will be identified.

H L A molecules are receptors on antigen presenting cells that present the antigen to the T cell, which starts an immune response. A variant may change the antigen binding site, so the molecule recognizes peptides that are not true antigens and starts an immune response against them. H L A variants change immune recognition, not how the drug is handled; they are not metabolism or transport variants. Polymorphisms in H L A B, H L A D Q and H L A D R are associated with many drug induced hypersensitivity reactions.

Each variant is tied to specific drugs. The two she emphasized are both H L A B: star fifty seven zero one with abacavir induced skin toxicity, which can be fatal, and star fifteen zero two with carbamazepine induced skin toxicity, also potentially fatal. Others are H L A B star fifty eight zero one with allopurinol skin toxicity, and an H L A D R B one, D R B five and D Q B one haplotype with amoxicillin clavulanate liver injury. How common these variants are varies across populations and is not yet well defined.
